tour.p1.s1.title: Start with a data review
tour.p1.s1.body: Review the loaded drillholes, validate their support, then prepare a reliable master for Assay.
tour.p1.s2.title: The sample needs validation
tour.p1.s2.body: This synthetic sample includes a missing collar, a missing geology log and a mismatched identifier. Validation identifies them; grades and missing values stay as recorded.
tour.p1.s3.title: Import your source tables
tour.p1.s3.body: Load collar, survey, assay and geology CSVs. Check automatic column assignments or assign columns manually before continuing.
tour.p1.s4.title: Resolve failures before geometry
tour.p1.s4.body: Read the failure and warning counts, inspect affected records and reconcile them with the source. Blocking errors must be resolved before Desurvey.
tour.p1.s5.title: Inspect the affected source
tour.p1.s5.body: These links open collar, survey, assay and geology directly. For the synthetic sample, download its source CSVs and reimport the corrected tables.
tour.p1.s6.title: Export after validation
tour.p1.s6.body: After validated Desurvey and Merge, export the master or send it to Assay. The PDF records data readiness and limitations; it does not certify geology.

flow.purpose10: Calculate interval coordinates using the recorded survey. Inspect the trajectory before merging.

flow.purpose13: Export the screening report and master data; continue the interpretation in Assay.

core.repair.title: Resolve validation findings
core.repair.scope: Correct measured source data before Desurvey. Missing measurements are never invented. Manual edits are applied with Apply changes and recorded in the activity log.
core.repair.confirm: Restore collar and geology from the bundled synthetic source? Assay grades and measured survey rows will be preserved. This action is recorded and can be undone before further edits.
core.repair.changed: The project changed. Review the current data before applying or undoing a repair.
core.repair.sourcePreview: The bundled original source contains the missing collar, missing geology log and the correct geology ID. Preview the findings above; automatic restoration uses these known records, with an audit and Undo.
core.repair.applied: Synthetic source restored. Validation refreshed; recompute downstream geometry.
core.repair.linkage: Compare the exact hole ID with Collar. Correct a verified ID or import the missing source record; do not guess a match.
core.repair.duplicate: Review the repeated collar ID. Keep the verified source record; conflicting coordinates require source confirmation.
core.repair.crs: Declare and use projected metre coordinates for desurvey. Verify the CRS and reproject from the source; degrees are not metres.
core.repair.interval: Review FROM/TO and overlapping intervals against the source. No interval is shortened or deleted automatically.
core.repair.measurement: Inspect missing or invalid required measurements. Edit verified values or import corrected source rows; use manual column assignment if a header was mapped incorrectly.
core.domain.invalidState: Domain interpretation could not be restored for the current source. Raw drillhole tables remain available.
core.repair.exportBlocked: Resolve blocking validation findings before exporting a clean handoff. Raw source tables remain available for correction.

core.renderDesurvey.assumedStart: Vertical direction assumed before the first measured survey
core.renderDesurvey.noSurvey: No measured survey: vertical screening assumption
core.renderDesurvey.lastExtension: Straight extension of the last measured direction
core.renderDesurvey.invalidTrajectory: These survey records do not define a usable trajectory. Correct the missing, out-of-range or conflicting measurements in Survey.
core.repair.warning.missingGeology: No geology log is loaded for {n} collar holes. Confirm whether geology logging is complete before interpreting domains.
core.repair.warning.missingSurvey: No measured directional survey is loaded for {n} collar holes. Review the vertical or last-direction assumption before using desurveyed positions.
core.repair.warning.missingAssay: No assay intervals are loaded for {n} collar holes.
core.repair.warning.providedXYZ: Coordinate source: supplied assay-interval midpoint XYZ; these coordinates are not independently surveyed here.
core.repair.warning.minimumCurvature: Coordinate source: Minimum-curvature desurvey using the measured directional survey.
core.repair.blocked: Resolve the blocking findings below before Desurvey. Each action opens the affected record.
core.repair.ready: No blocking findings. Review any warnings before continuing.
core.repair.noHoleMatches: No affected hole IDs match this search.
core.repair.editInstructions: Only the affected records are shown. Edit the highlighted cell using the verified source value, then click Apply changes. Return here to validate again.
core.repair.missingInstructions: No record exists for this exact ID in this table. Add the verified source record or import a corrected CSV. Only the ID can be prefilled; measurements stay empty.
core.repair.reason.missing-collar: This ID appears in the source tables but has no matching collar. Inspect its spelling in those records, or add the measured collar from the original source. The software cannot infer X, Y or Z.
core.repair.reason.missing-table: The collar ID exists, but no {table} record matches it. Check the ID spelling or supply the original source records. A missing geology log is a warning, not a fabricated lithology.
core.repair.reason.duplicate: Compare the original source entries for this ID. Correct a verified ID or delete the duplicate explicitly; conflicting coordinates cannot be chosen automatically.
core.repair.reason.crs: Verify the original CRS and reproject coordinates into metres. Correct column mapping if latitude/longitude was assigned to easting/northing.
core.repair.reason.completeness: The listed cells are empty. Fill verified source values, or correct the column mapping if data was assigned to the wrong field.
core.repair.reason.measurement: The listed measured values fail the structural limits. Edit the indicated fields against the original source; grades and angles are not guessed.
core.repair.reason.final-depth: Enter measured final depth if it is available. The value may remain missing with a recorded warning when measured survey geometry is usable.
core.repair.reason.directions: Stations at the same depth conflict or consecutive directions are opposite. Compare the source station values; the affected trace stays blocked until corrected.
core.repair.reason.gaps: Review the boundaries of this interval and its preceding interval. A gap may be intentional; the software does not invent an assay.
core.repair.reason.overlaps: Compare FROM/TO with the preceding interval. Correct the verified boundaries or remove a confirmed duplicate explicitly.
core.repair.reason.bdl: Negative grades may be laboratory detection-limit codes. Review the lab convention and choose BDL handling in Assay; they are not automatically replaced.
core.repair.reason.geometry: Desurvey needs finite measured coordinates. Fill the listed original coordinate values or correct their mapping; missing coordinates never become zero.
core.repair.appliedReview: Changes applied and recorded. Return to validation to check the current source, then recalculate downstream geometry.
core.repair.reason.missing-input: Import the missing measured source tables or review the coordinate-source mode. There is no source record to locate yet; geometry cannot be inferred.
core.repair.pdfScope: {n} cell changes recorded; measurements come from the reviewed source.
core.repair.pdfLimit: The most recent {n} cell changes are shown. Export the .orebit project for the complete correction audit.
core.repair.draftInstructions: This new record is a draft. Fill the highlighted fields from verified measurements, then apply and revalidate. Empty measurements are not estimated.
core.repair.linkedFinding: This record is linked to the finding above. Correct the highlighted value, apply changes, then revalidate.
core.scope.title: Continue with valid data
core.scope.preview: Keep {holes} holes / {assays} assay intervals; exclude {excluded} source records.
core.scope.policy: Entire affected holes are excluded, including their valid-looking intervals. Raw data and unresolved regional findings remain saved. This is a scoped screening result, not a full clean dataset.
core.scope.changed: Source data changed. Return to Validation and preview the scope again.
core.scope.none: No validated analysis population remains. Correct the source findings first.
core.scope.active: Scoped screening: {holes} holes / {assays} intervals; {excluded} source records excluded.
core.scope.regional: Full regional population; no validation exclusions
core.scope.limited: Showing the first 200 source records. Download the full exclusions CSV; the complete scope is saved in the project.
core.projectManager.title: Project Manager
panel.domain.title: Domain
dom.hint: Inspect measured drillhole geometry, choose geological contacts, then build or digitize an explicit solid. Source tables remain unchanged.
core.edaReference.title: Assay EDA reference
core.edaReference.returnCheckpoint: Return Assay checkpoint and validated geology
core.edaReference.returned: Checkpoint and validated geology were returned to Assay without reimporting rows.
core.edaReference.returnRecovery: Assay did not acknowledge the return. A recovery JSON was saved when possible.
core.edaReference.current: Source revision matches. Candidate awaits geological review.
core.edaReference.summary-only: Packet was compacted for size; intervals are examples only. Open Assay for the full proposal.
core.edaReference.stale: Source revision differs. This candidate is stale and cannot be accepted.
core.edaReference.referenceOnly: Source labels and interval endpoints are reference-only; Core assay/geology tables were not changed.
core.edaReference.accepted: Accepted as geological review input; source labels were not applied.
core.edaReference.declined: Proposal declined; source tables remain intact.
core.edaReference.loadedStale: EDA reference loaded but is stale for this source.
dom.canvasLabel: Drillhole intervals drawn in plan or section
dom.noData: No intervals to draw yet. Load collar, survey and the selected interval table first.
dom.noEndpoints: This dataset supplies interval midpoints only. The viewer needs from/to endpoints from a survey desurvey, so it draws nothing rather than guessing them.
dom.status: {holes} holes · {shown} of {inView} intervals drawn ({total} in table, {skipped} without endpoints)
dom.thinned: Display thinned to every {stride}th interval for speed; statistics and exports still use every interval.
dom.thinOffer: Drawing took {ms} ms. Thin the display for speed
dom.laterWhy: Reviewed solids export in project coordinates. Section CSV is available for accepted lofts. Resource support, density and estimation remain separate review decisions.
dom.tree.title: Domains
dom.tree.empty: No geological domains are defined yet. Group logged lithologies to start.
dom.toggleKey: Show or hide in the view (display only)
dom.digitizeWhy: Click the section to add a point. Contacts within the snap radius are used exactly.
dom.contact.title: Contact surface
dom.contact.choose: Choose a code or grade column
dom.contact.maxEdgeHelp: Blank uses 2.5 × median XY nearest-neighbour spacing; the actual limit appears in the contact result. This controls which TIN triangles are supported, not ground elevation. The limit is saved with each surface. To change it later, save a reviewed surface under a new name and select that surface when building the solid. No single distance is correct for every deposit.
dom.contact.prompt: Choose a domain to pick one contact per hole. The tables are not changed.
dom.contact.result.surface: Surface drawn only inside the contact hull and within the longest edge.
dom.contact.result.no-triangles: No triangle fits within the longest edge. Increase it only if the geology supports it.
dom.contact.result.insufficient: Fewer than 3 holes have a contact, so no surface is drawn.
dom.contact.result.ambiguous: The target occurs in separate intervals or across unsupported gaps. First/last surfaces would bridge the intervening material, so this build is blocked. Interpret each body in sections instead.
dom.contact.reason.repeated-domain-inter: target reappears after another logged unit
dom.contact.reason.domain-support-gap: an unknown or unsampled gap separates target intervals
dom.solid.result.ambiguous: No solid was built: separate or unsupported target intervals cannot be joined by one first/last envelope. Return to Contacts to inspect the named holes and choose section interpretation.
dom.contact.reason.unlogged-before-conta: unlogged or unsampled above the contact
dom.contact.reason.unlogged-no-member: unlogged intervals and no domain interval
dom.contact.reason.no-member-interval: no domain interval in this hole
dom.contact.reason.no-endpoint: no desurveyed endpoint at the contact
dom.contact.reason.starts-in-domain: already in grade at the first sample
dom.contact.reason.domain-reaches-end-of: domain continues to the end of hole
dom.solid.review: I checked this solid against the logs and sections.
dom.solid.acceptGeometry: A geometry check failed, so this solid cannot be accepted.
dom.solid.acceptTopo: Select collar elevations and pass the topography check before accepting. With no ground-surface source, this solid remains a preview.
dom.solid.accepted: Accepted as {code} ({volume} m³) and saved with the project. Resource requires its own support and estimation review.
dom.solid.title: Build and review solid
dom.solid.topo.help: Ground is a separate check, not the lower boundary. Collar elevations approximate the land surface; this check does not clip the solid to surveyed terrain.
dom.solid.topo.importedHelp: This solid uses the selected imported terrain TIN. The full XY footprint and every solid vertex must pass terrain coverage and elevation checks before acceptance.
dom.workflow.label: Domain workflow
dom.solid.basisTitle: How the top and base are chosen
dom.solid.basis: The top follows the selected contact rule (or the first interval top); the base follows the last interval base. Ground-surface checks do not change these geological limits.
dom.workflow.exportHelp: Send the master data and interpretation to Assay from Core Export, then continue in Resource. Review and apply Resource block support separately before estimation.
dom.solid.topoLabel: Ground check source (not the lower boundary)
dom.solid.prompt: Choose a domain under Contacts, select a ground-surface source, then build. Review the geometry checks before accepting the solid.
dom.solid.result.solid: Closed solid built. Select 3D in the viewer to inspect its shape, then review the checks and accept it below to save it. Until accepted it remains a preview.
dom.solid.result.invalid: Build rejected: geometry checks failed below. Review source intervals, contact coverage and triangle spacing before rebuilding. The candidate volume is not validated; do not accept it.
dom.solid.result.inverted: The base lies above the top in the holes listed. No solid was built.
dom.solid.result.pinched: The top and base meet in the holes listed. No solid was built; pinch-out end rules come with section loft.
dom.solid.result.insufficient: Fewer than 3 holes have both a top and a base, so no solid was built.
dom.solid.result.no-surface: The top or the base has no surface, so no solid was built.
dom.solid.result.no-triangles: No triangle fits within the longest edge, so no solid was built.
dom.contact.err.DOMAIN_SURFACE_MULTIVALU: two contacts share one easting and northing at different elevations, so one surface cannot hold both
dom.contact.err.DOMAIN_TIN_COLLINEAR: the contacts lie on one line
dom.contact.err.DOMAIN_TIN_INPUT: more than 2,000 contacts; filter the holes first
dom.dxf.err: Solid DXF export needs a validated solid.
dom.loft.title: Section loft
dom.loft.prompt: Choose Digitize, then click the section to outline the domain. Click the first point or Close ring to finish. One ring per section.
dom.loft.notSection: Open a section to digitize. Sections must be parallel, so keep the same azimuth.
dom.loft.draft: {n} points on this section. Close the ring when the outline is complete.
dom.loft.needTopo: Choose the ground-surface source beside Build loft.
dom.zoom.title: Section zoom
dom.zoom.help: Wheel: zoom at cursor · Alt + drag: pan · Keyboard: + / − / 0. View only; ring coordinates are unchanged.
dom.loft.end.zero: Zero: stop at the end sections
dom.loft.end.pinch: Pinch: close to a point at half the spacing
dom.loft.offPlane: Largest snapped contact distance from its section
dom.loft.outside: Vertices outside the collar surface (not checked)
dom.loft.err.DOMAIN_POLYGON_DUPLICATE: two consecutive points are the same
dom.loft.err.DOMAIN_LOFT_NOT_PARALLEL: the sections are not parallel; use one azimuth for every section
dom.loft.err.DOMAIN_LOFT_STATION_DUPLICA: two rings sit on the same section
dom.loft.err.DOMAIN_LOFT_CAP: an end section could not be closed
dom.loft.err.DOMAIN_LOFT_BUDGET: too many points for one loft
dom.loft.err.DOMAIN_TIN_COLLINEAR: the collars lie on one line, so topography cannot be checked
dom.loft.editPrompt: Select a point on the section or in the list. Edit its distance/RL, then Apply. Invalid polygons keep their previous shape.
dom.solid.overlapError: Overlaps {code} by {volume} m³. Inspect the sections and edit the boundaries; the accepted domains were retained.
dom.loft.newDomainConfirm: Start a new section interpretation? Accepted domains are retained. Select a defined domain to resume its draft; an unnamed draft can be restored with Undo.
dom.book.title: Geological groups · optional
dom.book.hint: Optional groups define lithology membership, not geometry. Save selects the group as Contact source; you may also use a logged lithology directly.
dom.book.label: Display name
dom.book.removeConfirm: Remove this geological group? Solids using it will need review.
dom.book.invalid: Enter a unique code, choose at least one lithology, and check density and precedence.
dom.solid.staleReview: Rebuild and review this domain before exporting it. Its saved volume is historical.
dom.noWebgl: 3D is unavailable in this browser. Inspect the same geometry in Plan or Section; data and modelling parameters are unchanged.
dom.loft.vertexManual: Use as manual vertex · remove snap link
dom.loft.anchorIssues: Anchors needing review · Edit and resnap or explicitly use a manual vertex
dom.loft.needRings: Closed section rings: {n}/2 minimum. Digitize on two different parallel sections and close each ring.
dom.loft.finishDraft: Close or clear the unfinished ring before building.
dom.loft.needEnd: Choose an end rule to define how the solid ends beyond the outer sections.
dom.loft.ready: Ready to build from the closed section rings. Then review the volume and validation checks.
dom.workflow.guide.contacts: Choose a geological unit and contact rule to generate each named surface; assign saved upper/lower surfaces under Build & review. The one-unit first/last option remains available.
dom.workflow.guide.loft: Choose the section azimuth in Plan or Section, then digitize and close rings on at least two sections with parallel planes. Loft orders rings by physical station, not click order. Review the end rule, ground check and geometry before acceptance. Saved rings keep their original planes.
dom.methodChoice.title: Choose how to interpret the solid
dom.methodChoice.sectionsHelp: Close a ring on section A and B, then loft and triangulate between them. Review the end rule and surface limit.
dom.methodChoice.surfacesHelp: Choose the geological unit and its top/base contacts. Build a TIN and close the supported volume between the contacts.
dom.methodChoice.limit: Current surfaces come from interpreted drillhole contacts. Arbitrary top/base surface import with complete clipping is planned; collar ground checks are approximate.
dom.surfaceImport.title: DXF terrain surface preview
dom.surfaceImport.limit: Preview only. This surface is not active terrain and does not clip a domain until coverage and clipping acceptance is complete.
dom.surfaceImport.preview: Validated preview: {vertices} vertices, {triangles} triangles; X {xmin}–{xmax}, Y {ymin}–{ymax}, Z {zmin}–{zmax} m; {crs}; SHA-256 {hash}. Coverage not assessed; model unchanged.
dom.surfaceImport.noTarget: Coverage not assessed: no current reviewed solid is available as a target.
dom.surfaceImport.use: Use this terrain for the next solid build
dom.surfaceImport.selected: Imported terrain selected as the next solid build input. Build coverage and elevation checks are still required.
flow.desurveyStatus: {holes} drillhole trajectories available · {fail} failed checks in the full source dataset. Inspect the trajectories and any recorded screening exclusions before handoff.
flow.mergeStatus: {rows} prepared intervals. Review coordinates, grades and geological associations before export.
dom.solid.reviewRequired: Enter the reviewer and rationale, then confirm that you inspected this solid.
dom.insight.empty: No assay or geological intervals are loaded. Import interval sources before interpreting a geological domain.
dom.insight.draft: Geological groups: {groups}. Define the interpretation, then Build and explicitly review the candidate; no reviewed solid is available yet.
dom.insight.candidate: Geological groups: {groups} · Built candidate: {volume} m³. Awaiting reviewer and rationale; this candidate is not approved for handoff.
dom.insight.ready: Geological groups: {groups} · Review recorded for solid: {volume} m³. Geometry is current; Resource support and estimation review remain separate.
dom.insight.stale: The previous interpretation or review is stale. Check current sources, rebuild and review before geometry handoff.
dom.insight.invalid: Candidate geometry needs correction. Check source coordinates and geometry validation before Build and review.
dom.insight.candidateReviewed: Geological groups: {groups} · Built candidate: {volume} m³, awaiting review. Earlier reviewed geometry: {reviewed} m³ remains separate; the new candidate is not approved for handoff.
dom.solid.savedView: Saved solid {code}. Select 3D in the viewer to inspect its shape; ensure its Visible checkbox is on. Plan shows drillhole intervals and contacts.
dom.solid.savedStale: Saved geometry for {code} is stale. Rebuild and review it before use; switching to 3D does not validate it.
dom.surfaceLibrary.title: Named contact surfaces
dom.surfaceLibrary.help: Choose a contact rule and source above, then save a named surface. Saved surfaces are boundaries, not accepted solids.
dom.surfaceLibrary.name: Surface name
dom.surfaceLibrary.saved: Surface saved. Create another boundary or choose two surfaces under Build & review.
dom.surfacePair.mode.interval: First and last contacts of one unit
dom.surfacePair.help: Names do not determine order. Choose the geological upper and lower surfaces and name the resulting solid; an optional geological group does not automatically select its boundaries. Only their common supported area is used. Inverted or crossing surfaces are rejected; no extrapolation is added.
dom.surfacePair.result.inverted: The lower surface lies above the upper surface within their shared support. Inspect the assignments or swap them explicitly; no solid was built.
dom.surfacePair.result.pinched: The surfaces meet within their shared support. A closed body with positive thickness is required; no solid was built. Review the interpretation.
dom.surfacePair.result.no-triangles: The surfaces have no common supported area. Inspect their coverage and edge limits; no extrapolation or solid was generated.
dom.surfacePair.fragmented: Contact coverage forms touching or disconnected patches, not one closed shell. Review both interpolation limits or interpret separate bodies. Self-intersection has not been checked.
dom.surfacePair.invalidDetail: The candidate was not accepted. Inspect the geometry diagnostic before rebuilding:
dom.surfacePair.supportJunctions: Support boundary touches itself at {n} XY locations (m): {points}. Inspect these contacts in plan/section. Review both surface interpolation limits only when geology supports the coverage; otherwise interpret separate bodies with sections. Changing terrain does not repair this topology.
dom.surfacePair.reviewSupport: Review contact coverage and interpolation limit →
dom.surfacePair.settingsHelp: Each surface keeps its own interpolation limit from Contacts → Longest triangle edge. These are already the applied limits, even if you left the input blank. Review the coverage in plan/section; changing ground source will not join disconnected patches. After changing a limit, save a new surface and select it above. No automatic extension or geological acceptance is applied.
dom.surfacePair.previewHelp: Two geological surfaces are enough to preview the solid geometry. A ground reference is a separate acceptance check, not a third boundary. Without that check you can inspect geometry, but cannot accept or hand off a validated domain.
dom.contact.boundaryHelp: Choose Top or Bottom of one continuous occurrence. Repeated bodies or data gaps need section interpretation; never join the first top to the last bottom.
dom.section.planHelp: Click a line to open its section. XS +00 is the data-centre plane; steps use 2 × half-width. Azimuth is clockwise from North. Saved rings keep their planes.
core.ex.populationHelp: This screen exports the current merged intervals, with their recorded edits and analysis scope. Optional Core composites have a separate download in Composite. Continue in Assay sends merged intervals for EDA; final domain-constrained compositing is reviewed in Assay before Resource.
